what_this_is: Defensive positional adjustments re-estimated from Baseball-Reference's own construction rather than taken from the folklore table. Least squares of BRef runs_position per 650 PA on per-row innings shares, no intercept, recentred so the exposure-weighted sum over all nine positions is zero.
important: This is an INVERSION, not an independent measure of defensive difficulty. A rung reads as what Baseball-Reference PRICES that position at. For work that rides the bWAR frame (eWAR) that is the feature; for a from-scratch defensive model it is a constraint.
units: runs per 650 PA, relative to the league average defensive position
method: least squares of BRef runs_position/650PA on innings shares, no intercept, recentred to exposure-weighted sum zero

values.use_for: everything that rides the bWAR frame, including eWAR; this is what every internal valuation uses

values_fielder_centred.use_for: comparison against the published folklore table, whose eight fielders also sum to zero with DH outside it

bases.note: the two differ by one constant, so every gap between two positions is identical in both

identification.zero_means: the average defensive position of a qualified player-season, every fitted player-season counted once: the weights are the column means of the per-row innings shares, not league innings totals
identification.uncentred_level_equals: mean(runs_position per 650 PA) over the fitted rows
identification.why_equal_weight_sums_are_not_zero: DH is 8.8% of exposure, not a ninth, so equal-weighting the nine rungs over-counts the DH penalty; and with the exposure-weighted sum pinned at zero the eight fielding rungs must sum to -8 x w_DH x L_DH / (1 - w_DH). Only the exposure-weighted sum is a constraint - the other two are consequences of it.

fit.dh_exposure_spec: residual: max(0, PA x inn_per_pa - fielded innings)

basis.caveat: the folklore table is quoted per 162 games in some sources and per 600-700 PA in others, and it is the FanGraphs/Tango ladder while this fit inverts Baseball-Reference, so both columns are published and neither is presented as the answer

folklore_comparison.read_this: the folklore table is quoted per full defensive season and ours per 650 PA of exposure, so subtracting them directly overstates folklore by about 14 percent. Both the raw and the rescaled comparison are published and neither is presented as the answer: the convention is ambiguous across sources, and the folklore ladder is FanGraphs/Tango while this fit inverts Baseball-Reference.
